correctness.rationale: For all indicated spherical parameters, the Legendre angular integral is L1. Its t-Fourier integral and theta integral are explicit beta integrals with absolute Fubini and yield the stated positive gamma product. Principal parameters yield conjugate beta factors; real complementary parameters each yield positive gamma-modulus factors. Standard SO(2)-spherical unitary dual consists of trivial, complementary and principal sectors. For an arbitrary L1 spherical Bochner mixture, principal part is uniformly L1, trivial mass contradicts integrability and nonnegative complementary part is L1 by subtraction; Tonelli then gives an integral of strictly positive densities over a nonzero positive measure. Boundary normalization and three numerical Fourier samples were independently checked. No infinite conclusion rests on finite sampling.

originality.rationale: The contemporary full-text arXiv:2606.07286 establishes principal spherical Fourier positivity but explicitly excludes complementary series from its theorem and its arbitrary-mixture corollary. The new result includes all pure-complementary and mixed L1 spherical measures for SL2(R), established by a separate positive beta-product and Tonelli argument. Actual indexed literature searches for rank-one complementary positivity and Legendre gamma transforms found no directly covering mathematical record; several closest ranked records concern SU(2) partial sums, Legendre minimizer problems, and spherical harmonic concentration, none implying this statement. Residual coverage risk from historical special-function tables or unindexed earlier rank-one positivity remains substantive.
residual_risks: An old integral table could state the same gamma product and, combined with standard spherical dual theory, imply the all-spectrum consequence.
A not-yet-indexed companion article or earlier rank-one theorem may already treat complementary spectral measures.

value.rationale: This completes a whole natural real-rank-one case of an explicitly formulated 2026 split-torus positivity problem, including arbitrary pure-complementary and mixed spherical measures excluded by the motivating general principal-series theorem. Strictly positive Fourier density has interpretation as nonvanishing variance for abelian torus actions, and the theorem identifies the precise spectral hypothesis needed for all mixtures. The explicit density and all-spectrum conclusion are more than a routine finite test; higher-rank and nonsplit cases remain open.
